questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Most common isotopes of hydrogen (non-radioactive) is
questions.solution:
Protium $\left({ }_1^1 H\right)$ deuterium or heavy hydrogen $\left({ }_1^2 \mathrm{H}\right.$ or D$)$ and tritium $\left({ }_1^3 \mathrm{H}\right.$ or T $)$ are the isotopes of hydrogen.
Protium or ordinary hydrogen has one proton and no neutron in the nucleus and one electron revolves around the nucleus. It is the most abundant and common form of hydrogen (approximately $99.98 \%$ ).
${ }_1^2 \mathrm{H}+{ }_{\mathrm{l}}^2 \mathrm{H} \longrightarrow{ }_1^3 \mathrm{H}+{ }_1^1 \mathrm{H}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Number of hydrogen-bonded water molecules associated in $\mathrm{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is
questions.solution: Only one water molecule, which is outside the brackets (coordination sphere) is hydrogen bonded. The other four molecules of water are coordinated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen molecule differs from chlorine molecule in the following respect:
options: Hydrogen molecule is non-polar but chlorine molecule is polar
Hydrogen molecule is polar while chlorine molecule is non-polar
Hydrogen molecule can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds but chlorine molecule does not
Hydrogen molecule cannot participate in coordinate bond formation but chlorine molecule can
questions.solution: Hydrogen molecule contains no lone pair, hence not able to take part in coordinate bond formation but $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ can.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxide that gives $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ on treatment with dilute acid is
questions.solution: Peroxides give hydrogen peroxide, on treatment with dilute acids. Hence, only sodium peroxide $\left(\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{O}_2\right)$ will give $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following undergoes reduction with hydrogen peroxide in alkaline medium?
questions.solution:
It reduces iodine to iodide ion in alkaline medium.
$\begin{array}{r}\mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{~s})+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2(a q)+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \longrightarrow \\ 2 \mathrm{I}^{-}(a q)+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})+\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g})\end{array}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The melting point of solid substances is directly proportional to pressure acting on them. However, ice-melts at a temperature lower than its usual melting point, when the pressure increases. This is because
options: ice is not a true solid
ice is loss denser than water
questions.solution: Ice melts at a temperature lower than its usual melting point because ice is less denser than water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Moist hydrogen peroxide can not be dried over conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ because
questions.solution:
Conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ decomposes $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$, thus $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ can not be dried over it.
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2+[\mathrm{O}] \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hardness of water is due to presence of salts of :
questions.solution: Hardness of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is due to the presence of bicarbonates, chlorides, and sulphates of Ca and Mg ions.
